clue.text: They help one to see, for example, about you and the girls

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits around the old pronoun, enclosing it

parts.note: the usual abbreviation e.g. for 'for example'
ye is the archaic form of you
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Someone surveying a group of young women, with an aside about you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks like a link phrase but gives the abbreviation; 'about' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are lenses worn to correct sight, so they help a person see.

clue.text: Period of my early childhood

indicators.note: the start of life, here read as a run of letters lying inside the words my early

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a stage of their infancy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'mY EARly'; 'childhood' signals a word growing up inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months is a stretch of time, a common sense of period.

clue.text: Place left for shooting at

parts.note: Goa is a place, a state on India's west coast

explanation.surface: A spot set aside as a target range.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and hockey the net and posts are the target players aim at.

clue.text: Where industrious one is on edge

parts.note: the ant is proverbially hard-working
a rim is an edge; 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: Asking where a busy insect stands on a border.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county of Northern Ireland; 'Where' is the definition, a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A county is a location, so 'Where' points to a place name.

clue.text: Hostess who makes a team come to earth amid unusual delays

indicators.note: the run of pieces goes into the middle of the rearranged letters of delays
the letters of delays are taken in an unusual order

parts.note: a side is a team
to land is to come down to earth

explanation.surface: A hostess whose team keeps coming back to ground despite strange delays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of delays into SELADY, and 'amid' splits that between its second and third letters to take the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman running a guest house at a resort is a host to holidaymakers.

clue.text: Soaked as the grass above the home

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the other, so it comes first

parts.note: sod is turf, grass with its roots
a den is a home or lair

explanation.surface: Turf over a house, damp through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaked is wet through, saturated.

clue.text: Old master caught being changed for modern artist

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase plus the cricket letter are being changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An Old Master painting caught and swapped for a modern work.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir William Coldstream was a twentieth-century British painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldstream painted in the twentieth century, a modern painter.

clue.text: Relative holds one for writer

indicators.note: the word for a sibling holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: bro, short for brother, is a relative
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A family member holding something for a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint pen is a writing instrument, so it is a writer.

clue.text: Examiners sip cornets when they are runny

indicators.note: melting ice creams run, so their letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: Officials sipping ice-cream cones as they melt.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors examine things officially, so they are examiners.

clue.text: A wise man with space for flowers has these pioneers at heart

indicators.note: only the heart of the combined words is kept, losing their first and last letters

parts.note: a savant is a learned, wise man
a garden is a space for growing flowers

explanation.surface: A sage with a flower bed who has pioneers dear to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' strips the first and last letters from SAVANTGARDEN, leaving the core. The 'A' at the start is only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The avant-garde are innovators who lead the way in the arts.

clue.text: Was accustomed to be employed

definitions.meaning: in '... to', the word means was in the habit of

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a past habit and something put into service.

clue.text: Sailor I class as a spider

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor
a grade is a class or rank

explanation.surface: A sailor classing himself as a spider.
explanation.walkthrough: A saltigrade spider is a jumping spider.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltigrade describes jumping spiders, so it names a kind of arachnid.

clue.text: Went into the water carrying a fish but got separated

indicators.note: the verb for plunging carries the fish inside it

parts.note: dived means plunged into the water
the ide, also spelt id, is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A diver who caught a fish but became detached.
explanation.definitionFit: Things divided have been split apart, separated.

clue.text: Etiquette is an instrument for keeping company to the point

indicators.note: the instrument keeps the other pieces held inside it

parts.note: a drum is a musical instrument

indicators.note: company is attached to the point, so it follows it

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Etiquette described as an instrument for keeping a firm on topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the point' looks like 'relevant', but it places the company after the compass point; 'for keeping' then puts ECO inside the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper behaviour, the rules of polite conduct.

clue.text: Illness which would make one pass away if one didn't take the waters

indicators.note: to take in is to contain, so the word for dying takes the waters inside

parts.note: to die is to pass away
the seas are the waters

explanation.surface: An ailment that would kill one if one did not go to a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' signals the enclosure; with the waters removed only the word for dying is left, hence the spa joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is a sickness, an illness.

clue.text: Girl made free with what a princess wears

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the letters of made are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: A girl taking liberties with a princess's headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges the word made into ADEM, which follows the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crown or headband is worn by royalty.

clue.text: Hard labour is a vital occupation for an academic

indicators.note: the vital occupation is set down for the academic, who comes first

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
key means vital, crucial
work is an occupation

explanation.surface: A claim that hard graft is an essential job for a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is tedious heavy toil, the grinding part of any job.

clue.text: Refreshments included by those who keep open house are most attractive

indicators.note: the refreshments are included inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the National Trust, NT, opens historic houses to the public
ices are frozen refreshments

explanation.surface: Snacks provided by generous hosts are the most appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that runs stately homes open to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicest means most pleasing, the most attractive.

clue.text: Where one plays for one's country?

definitions.text: Where one plays for one's country?

parts.words: Where one plays for one's country?
parts.note: sounds like an international sports venue, but 'plays' means performs drama on the nation's own stage

explanation.definitionFit: London's state-funded playhouse on the South Bank stages drama on the nation's behalf.

clue.text: Reward for playing at the Oval is a food container

definitions.text: Reward for playing at the Oval
definitions.meaning: a cup is a trophy, and the oval shape is the egg's, read as a prize for playing 'at the Oval'
a small holder for a boiled egg at table

explanation.definitionFit: A breakfast holder for a boiled egg, playfully seen as a trophy for the egg-shaped.

clue.text: Important building where one article has to be in position

indicators.note: the article has to go in among the letters of the position word

parts.note: a place is a position
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grand building where each item must be in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand official residence, an important building.

clue.text: It is about right that religious retreat is a fraud

indicators.note: the fraud goes around the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a sham is a fraud

explanation.surface: Someone suggesting a spiritual retreat is bogus.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage, a place of spiritual retreat.

clue.text: Swear during a game?

parts.note: at can mean during, as in 'at night'
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Cursing in the middle of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare on oath, to swear.

clue.text: Charge made for fruit on the island

indicators.note: the fruit is put on after the island

parts.note: the Isle of Man
a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: A fee charged for fruit sold on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official commission or instruction, a charge.

clue.text: River Don?

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham in north-east England
to don is to put on clothing

explanation.definitionFit: A north-east English river, and the verb meaning to put on or have on clothes.

clue.text: Deadly hill

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means fierce or lethal
a hill or moor in northern England

explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective meaning ruthless, and a northern English word for an upland.

clue.text: Male presenting a play without gin in it

indicators.note: the drink's letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: staging a play is presenting it

explanation.surface: A man putting on a show with no gin involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and by extension a man alone.

clue.text: Those who run the club cannot quite make a game with ten men

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new
the word game is not quite complete, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A club's bosses failing to field a side of eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cannot quite' cuts GAME to GAM; 'make' rearranges A GAM TEN MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The managers of a club, as a body, are its management.

clue.text: Got up, we hear, as lots of eggs

indicators.note: signals a word said out loud

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, got up

explanation.surface: Someone getting up and noticing a heap of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is fish spawn, masses of eggs.

clue.text: You go back without a servant to record the subject

indicators.note: the turned pronoun goes outside, round the servant and record
the archaic pronoun goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: ye is the archaic you
a gyp is a college servant at Cambridge
a log is a record

explanation.surface: Telling someone to turn back without a servant to note things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns the archaic pronoun into EY; 'without' puts it outside the rest. A gyp is a Cambridge college servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of ancient Egypt is an academic discipline, a subject.
